title: Nokia 123 Shield Brings Water Resistance and 19-Day Battery for Under ₹2,500
excerpt: HMD's latest Nokia-branded feature phone targets outdoor workers and budget buyers with dust and water protection, USB-C charging, and marathon standby life — but its 2G-only connectivity limits where it can be used.
body:
• HMD has unveiled the Nokia 123 Shield, its most affordable water and dust-resistant feature phone, priced at ₹2,499 in India and between €35–€40 in European retail listings.
  • The phone features a removable 1,750 mAh battery that delivers up to 19 days of standby and 27.9 hours of talk time, along with USB-C charging and a MicroSD card slot.
  • The Nokia 123 Shield is limited to 2G networks only, which could restrict its usefulness as 2G shutdowns continue worldwide.

HMD has added a new entry to its Nokia-branded feature phone lineup: the Nokia 123 Shield. The company calls it its "most affordable water and dust-resistant feature phone," built for people who work outdoors or need a cheap, durable backup device.

The phone has not received an official global price announcement yet. However, retail listings spotted in Bulgaria and Greece have placed it between €35 and €40, according to Gizmochina. In India, Smartprix lists the device at ₹2,499 with an "upcoming" availability tag.

What the Nokia 123 Shield Offers

The design is utilitarian. The phone has a textured plastic exterior along its sides for improved grip, and a rubber flap covers the ports on the bottom to keep water, sand, and dust out. Under the flap sit a USB-C port — a welcome upgrade over the Micro USB connectors still common in this price range — and a standard 3.5mm headphone jack.

"The company calls it its "most affordable water and dust-resistant feature phone," built for people who work outdoors or need a cheap, durable backup device."

Inside, the specifications are deliberately minimal. It runs on HMD's S30+ operating system, powered by a Unisoc SC6531E processor. Storage and RAM come in at just 4MB each, meaning anything beyond basic contacts and messages requires a MicroSD card, which the device supports up to 32GB. The 2.4-inch QVGA display handles the basics, and there is a low-resolution QVGA camera with an LED flash on the back.

Battery life is where the Nokia 123 Shield makes its case. The removable 1,750 mAh battery can deliver up to 27.9 hours of continuous talk time and up to 19 days on standby, according to HMD. For comparison, HMD's recently launched Nokia 210 4G and Nokia 200 4G feature phones promise up to 13 days of standby with their 1,450 mAh batteries, according to Digital Trends.

Practical Features for the Field

The Nokia 123 Shield includes an FM radio that works with or without wired headphones connected, and a built-in flashlight that HMD says is brighter than the one on the older Nokia 110 model. The phone supports dual Mini SIM cards and weighs 108 grams. It comes in two colors: green and purple.

The 2G Problem

There is a significant catch. The Nokia 123 Shield only supports 2G networks, operating on GSM 900 and 1800 bands. While HMD says the phone is optimized for reliable call quality and strong signal retention, the reality is that 2G networks are being phased out across much of the world.

In the United States, all major carriers have already shut down their 2G infrastructure. Several European operators have announced sunset timelines. India's 2G networks remain operational for now, but Reliance Jio never had a 2G network to begin with, and Airtel and Vodafone Idea have been gradually migrating users to 4G. For anyone in a market where 2G is disappearing, this phone could have a limited shelf life.

Where It Fits in HMD's Strategy

The Nokia 123 Shield arrives as HMD continues to balance two identities. On one hand, it is building its own HMD-branded smartphones targeting younger buyers. On the other, it is extending its Nokia licensing deal — reportedly now running through at least 2028–2029 — to keep the feature phone line alive.

HMD recently launched four Nokia-branded 4G feature phones with AI assistant buttons and USB-C charging. The 123 Shield sits below those models in both price and capability, aiming squarely at buyers who prioritize durability and battery life over connectivity.

What to Watch

HMD has not announced specific launch dates or availability beyond the European retail sightings. For Indian buyers, the ₹2,499 price point would place the Nokia 123 Shield among the cheapest water-resistant phones on the market — if it arrives before 2G networks become too unreliable to depend on.
